rationale: F95 addresses a P0 UX gap: new users land on empty pages with no guidance, which directly impacts retention. The feature is frontend-only (no backend changes, no DB migrations, no provider integration), making it low-risk and self-contained. It consolidates inconsistent empty states into a shared EmptyState component, reducing tech debt. The i18n infrastructure is already mature (215+ keys, EN+PT-BR). localStorage-based first-login detection is simple and reliable. With 1477 frontend tests and established component patterns, this is a safe, high-value improvement. No blocking dependencies.

pros: Fixes critical new-user experience gap (no onboarding exists today)
Frontend-only — zero risk to backend, database, or providers
Creates reusable EmptyState component that reduces future tech debt
Leverages existing i18n, Tailwind theme, and component patterns
High user impact relative to low implementation complexity
cons: Adds ~30-50 i18n keys across two locales
Requires touching multiple pages to migrate existing empty states

pros: Could bundle with a larger UX overhaul later
cons: Every new user hitting empty pages without guidance is a retention loss
The longer it waits, the more inconsistent empty states accumulate
No upcoming features would conflict or benefit from deferral
